title: Chemical Bonding I (Ionic & Covalent) - Chemistry - Nature of Bonds
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Fundamentally, why do atoms form chemical bonds?
options: To increase their potential energy and become more reactive.
To lower their potential energy and become more stable.
To increase the number of electrons in the nucleus.
questions.explain: Atoms form bonds because the resulting compound is more stable (has lower potential energy) than the separate atoms. This usually involves achieving a stable electron configuration.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the primary difference between ionic and covalent bonding?
options: Ionic bonding involves the sharing of electrons, while covalent bonding involves the transfer of electrons.
Ionic bonding occurs between two nonmetals, while covalent bonding occurs between a metal and a nonmetal.
Ionic bonding involves the electrostatic attraction between ions formed by electron transfer, while covalent bonding involves the sharing of electrons.
Ionic bonds are directional, whereas covalent bonds are non-directional.
questions.explain: Ionic bonding is characterized by the transfer of electrons creating ions held together by electrostatic forces. Covalent bonding involves the sharing of valence electrons between atoms.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: In the potential energy curve for the formation of a bond between two hydrogen atoms, what does the minimum point of the curve represent?
options: The point of maximum repulsion between nuclei.
The bond length where the system is most stable.
The point where the atoms are infinitely separated.
The point where the kinetic energy is zero.
questions.explain: The minimum on the potential energy diagram corresponds to the equilibrium bond distance (bond length) where the attractive and repulsive forces balance, and the potential energy is lowest.
